overview_classification.summary_label_zh: Module-LWE 格基、签名型双向认证三消息 AKE

authentication.mechanism: Both parties sign the role- and identity-bound transcript hash with pre-distributed long-term signature keys.

roles.key_details: Holds a long-term signature key pair and creates the per-session DKE key pair (M1, sk_e).
Holds a long-term signature key pair and samples fresh DKE response randomness per session.

pre_distributed_material: Certified initiator signature verification key pk_A
Certified responder signature verification key pk_B

forward_secrecy.conditions: Claimed in the CK model for fresh sessions; the tested session and matching session must not have their ephemeral state/session key revealed before completion.

protocol_characteristics.key_confirmation: No separate MAC-based key-confirmation value; the three-pass signed transcript provides mutual entity authentication, while the signatures do not directly cover the derived raw secret.
protocol_characteristics.transcript_binding: T = H(LABEL_A || LABEL_B || pk_A || pk_B || M1 || M2; N), and the final key is KDF(raw_ss || T).
protocol_characteristics.identity_binding: Both certified verification keys, role labels, and both DKE public messages are included in the signed transcript hash.

technical_classification.construction_paradigm: Three-pass signed ephemeral Ding-type key exchange: a CPA-secure reconciliation-based DKE is authenticated with two long-term signatures.

underlying_primitives.name: DKE
underlying_primitives.role: Ephemeral two-pass CPA-secure reconciliation key exchange

hard_problems.name: Module Learning With Errors (MLWE)
hard_problems.role: Secrecy of the DKE layer and part of ML-DSA security

hard_problems.name: Module Short Integer Solution (MSIS)
hard_problems.role: Unforgeability foundation of the ML-DSA authentication layer

security_models: Canetti-Krawczyk model with weak perfect forward secrecy

components.name: M1
components.semantics: Fresh initiator ephemeral DKE public key.

protocol_flow.semantics: The initiator creates (M1, sk_e), sends m1 = M1, and retains sk_e, M1, and pk_A.

components.name: M2
components.semantics: Responder DKE response containing compressed data and reconciliation signal.

components.name: sigma_B
components.semantics: Responder signature on transcript hash T.

protocol_flow.semantics: The responder computes the raw shared secret, transcript T, and sends m2 = M2 || sigma_B.

components.name: sigma_A
components.semantics: Initiator signature on the same transcript hash T.

protocol_flow.semantics: After verifying sigma_B and deriving the DKE secret, the initiator sends sigma_A; the responder verifies it before accepting.

static_contributions: Long-term signing keys authenticate T but are not inputs to the DKE raw secret.
ephemeral_contributions: Raw ss from DKE.Response(M1, rho_2) / DKE.DeriveSecret(M2, sk_e)
key_schedule.transcript_hash: T = H(LABEL_A || LABEL_B || pk_A || pk_B || M1 || M2; N)
key_schedule.session_key_derivation: session_key = KDF(ss || T; N) (the algorithms store state (ss,T) and apply KDF to that state).
key_schedule.domain_separation: Role- and level-specific LABEL_A and LABEL_B strings (DKEX-KSIG-...-A/B); SM3-256 at 128/256 and SM3 pseudoXOF-512 at 512.
key_schedule.ephemeral_secret_erasure: Initiator erases sk_e, M1, and pk_A from session state after deriving ss; the submission requires fresh single-use DKE secrets to prevent failure-reaction accumulation.

parameter_sets.name: DKEX-512
issues: The ML-DSA-87 authentication layer is explicitly limited to about 256 classical bits and does not meet the 512-bit confidentiality target.

correctness.relationship: A DKEX session has one DKE reconciliation event, so its honest-session failure probability is the underlying DKE delta, not twice delta.
correctness.basis: Algorithm specification Section 3.3, pp. 21-22; one fresh single-use DKE execution per session.

security_claims.claim: Mutual entity authentication follows from EUF-CMA security of both transcript signatures and collision resistance of the transcript hash.
Session-key security in the Canetti-Krawczyk model with weak perfect forward secrecy.
Key indistinguishability reduces to CPA security of ephemeral DKE, signature unforgeability, transcript hashing, and the KDF/random-oracle assumption.
Binding role labels, both certified verification keys, and both DKE messages in T is argued to prevent transcript misbinding and unknown-key-share patterns.

claimed_advantages.claim: Provides mutually authenticated CK/wPFS security while using a fresh CPA-secure DKE directly.
Separates the DKE arithmetic, signature authentication, transcript hashing, and KDF into modular components.
Uses ML-KEM-like module-lattice arithmetic and standardized ML-DSA authentication for the first two target levels.
Reference, AVX2, ARMv8-A, and Cortex-M4 implementations preserve the same wire formats.

limitations_and_constraints.description: Both parties' certified long-term signature verification keys must be available to their peers.
The reconciliation-based DKE has a nonzero honest-session failure probability delta.
The claimed wPFS depends on CK freshness and non-exposure of target ephemeral/session state.
DKEX-512 uses provisional ML-DSA-87, limiting authentication to about 256 classical bits although the DKE confidentiality target is 512 bits.
Security depends on CPA-secure DKE, EUF-CMA signatures, transcript-hash collision resistance, and the stated KDF/random-oracle assumptions.
Reference benchmarks use one Intel Core i9-10885H under Ubuntu 24.04/WSL2 and average 128 exchanges.
